1	# Email triage and newsflow redesign: plan
2	
3	Oct 8, 2026 · @Kelvin
4	
5	This is a build spec to be used by a coding agent. The prototype classifies each of 300 synthetic emails by how much attention it needs, then compares the relevant ones with a five-company book and suggests changes for an investment analyst to decide on.
6	
7	## Overview
8	
9	The design is settled and nothing is built yet. The hand-off is this spec, the corpus prompt and six generation prompts. The corpus, the seed files, the criteria files and all code are still to be produced.
10	
11	### Method
12	
13	[embedded content: proposed method · corpus and book in, brief and evaluation out\]
14	
15	Jev reads every email against the desk's relevance criteria and never sees the book. Two pathways follow the gate: attention notes for emails that need a person, and the analysis agent for emails that bear on a thesis. The analyst's decision is the only path by which the book changes.
16	The purpose of this is to automatically triage incoming emails for relevent research insights, identify those emails, and then parse research insights from the to be presented to an analyst.
17	
18	## Start here
19	
20	Build four things, in this order of importance:
21	
22	1. **A pipeline** that reads 300 synthetic emails and emits redundancy flags, triage labels, attention notes and thesis suggestions.
23	2. **A state layer:** criteria text files that users can read and extend, plus a driver model and a thesis for each of five companies, changed only when the analyst accepts a suggestion. This layer will also analyze and provide insight based on the emails.
24	3. **A web app:** morning brief, suggestion review, company pages, criteria viewer, audit view, raw inbox and eval page. This is to be done last.
25	
26	
27	### Inputs and who provides them
28	
29	| Input | Lands in | Provided by |
30	| --- | --- | --- |
31	| This spec | `SPEC.md` | Supplied: a Markdown export of this document. The agent reads it whole before step 0. |
32	| Corpus prompt | `docs/corpus_documentation/synthetic_data_prompt.md` | Supplied. Use only the text above its cut line; the appendix below it is for human reviewers. |
33	| Generation prompts | `prompts/` | Supplied: six prompts and a README that gives their order. |
34	| Test corpus: 600 emails, two days of 300 | `data/corpus/day_1/emails.jsonl`, `data/corpus/day_2/emails.jsonl` | Supplied, generated from the corpus prompt. The agent never generates or edits it. |
35	| Tuning corpus | `data/corpus/tuning/emails.jsonl` | Being generated separately from the corpus prompt. The agent never generates or edits it. |
36	| Book: stances, sizes, pillars, driver IDs, links | `data/seed/` | This spec, under "The book" and "State". Copy them exactly. |
37	| Book: driver values, consensus, bounds, multiples | `data/seed/models_draft.json` | The agent runs `prompts/01_book.prompt.md`; a person reviews the result. A script merges the draft into `models.json`. |
38	| Book: base revenue, tax rate, share count | `data/seed/models.json` | The agent takes them from each company's latest annual report. |
39	| Criteria starter rules | `criteria/*.md` | The agent runs `prompts/02_jev_criteria.prompt.md`; a person reviews the result. |
40	| Skills, stage instructions, tool definitions | `skills/`, `instructions/`, `tools/` | The agent runs prompts 04, 05 and 06; a person reviews the results. |
41	| API keys | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` for every generative model call; `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` for Jev, which OpenRouter does not serve. The Anthropic API is never called directly. | Supplied in `.env`, which is never committed. Never printed or logged. |
42	| Deploy host | Outside the repo | Supplied by the reviewer, with its credentials. |
43	
44	Every generated file is committed as a draft and listed in REVIEW.md before the pipeline is tuned on it.
45	
46	### Where a person is needed
47	
48	The agent never waits for a review. It stops only where this table says so.
49	
50	| When | What the person does | If the person is absent |
51	| --- | --- | --- |
52	| After step 0 | Reads the drafts listed in `REVIEW.md`: book numbers, criteria, skills, instructions and tools. | Continue on the drafts. `REVIEW.md` records which were unreviewed when tuning ran. |
53	| Before tuning | Supplies the tuning corpus at `data/corpus/tuning/emails.jsonl`. | Build and test everything else on the fixtures and both test days at starting values, and report that tuning is pending. |
54	| After step 6 | Fills in and commits the two review sheets. | The eval page shows the three hand reviews as pending. |
55	| At step 7 | Supplies a host and its credentials. | Deliver the container and the command that runs it locally. |
56	| After step 7 | Records the screencast and writes the summary. | Nothing in the build waits on this. |
57	
58	The final run is one pass of the pipeline and the eval script over each test day (`day_1`, then `day_2`), made after tuning is frozen.
59	
60	Two failures have their own rule. If the TypeSafe packages do not install, move them to an optional dependency group so `uv sync` passes, and continue with a fake client. If both Jev routes fail with a valid key, stop and report.
61	
62	Three more cases have a default. The lead runs each generation prompt with the analysis model through OpenRouter (`scripts/run_generation_prompt.py`), or in a fresh subagent, giving it only the text below the prompt's line, and notes the model in `REVIEW.md`. If DSPy itself does not install, call the model SDKs directly behind the same module interfaces. If the pages under "Read first" cannot be reached, follow the sketch under "Calling Jev".
63	
64	### Fixed decisions
65	
66	| Decision | Choice |
67	| --- | --- |
68	| Coverage | Amazon (AMZN), Nvidia (NVDA), Microsoft (MSFT), Apple (AAPL), Alphabet (GOOGL) |
69	| Corpus | Two days of 300 synthetic emails each from the corpus prompt, labeled without reference to any book |
70	| Book | A fictional example book in the seed files, kept separate from the corpus |
71	| Classification | Jev classifies every email by the attention it needs. It never sees the book. |
72	| Relevance criteria | Plain text files, one per label, hold the criteria Jev applies. Users can read, audit and add rules. They hold kinds of information, never views. |
73	| Redundancy | Every email is embedded and compared with every earlier email; a close match is flagged as potentially redundant |
74	| Attention pathway | Emails that need a person get a note with a summary, the reason and the action asked for |
75	| Analysis agent | A stronger model with two skills: how new information may alter an existing thesis, and whether it should spawn a new one |
76	| Who decides | Only the analyst. Models recommend and never make an investment decision. |
77	| Language | Python for everything, including a server-rendered UI; no TypeScript |
78	| Surface | Morning brief plus alerts; the inbox is untouched |
79	| Runtime | Pipeline output is precomputed and committed; one route runs live |
80	| Build time | 2–3 days |
81	
82	### Definition of done
83	
84	- From a clean clone, one command runs the pipeline over the corpus and writes its outputs.
85	- Every email has one triage label and a reason, and every flagged repeat points to the earlier email it resembles.
86	- Every email flagged for human attention has a note with a summary, a reason and the action asked for.
87	- Every suggestion shows its linked emails, and every quoted section exists verbatim in its source email.
88	- Accepting a thesis suggestion logs the evidence, and updating a linked assumption recomputes EPS and target price.
89	- Adding a rule to a criteria file and running the criteria check shows which emails changed label and how the scores moved.
90	- Every email not shown in the brief appears in the audit view with a reason.
91	- The eval page reports the pipeline's scores against the corpus labels.
92	- Every run writes token use and latency per stage, per model and per email, and the Monitor page shows them.
93	- The deployed URL works from a clean browser, and reset restores the seed state.
94	
95	## Why this exists
96	
97	A technology analyst at a long/short equity fund receives 100 to 300 emails a day. Most are noise, a few bear on a thesis, and a few need a person to act. Today that sorting is done from subject lines, and what is learned rarely reaches the thesis record.
98	
99	> How might we sort every inbound email by the attention it needs, then compare the relevant ones with the desk's book, so each day collapses to a few recommendations and requests, each with its evidence, and everything else is provably safe to ignore?
100	
101	### Design rules to preserve
102	
103	When the spec is silent, these seven rules decide.
104	
105	1. **Recommendations, not summaries.** Reading a relevant email produces a suggestion about a named thesis, with the email sections that support it, or a stated reason for none.
106	2. **Models recommend; the analyst decides.** No model makes an investment decision, writes to the book, does arithmetic or invents an ID. Code validates and computes.
107	3. **Classification never sees the book.** Jev gets one email and the desk's relevance criteria. It never gets positions, views or other emails.
108	4. **Every change is traceable.** State is the seed plus a log of accepted changes, each tied to quoted sections of emails.
109	5. **Nothing is hidden silently.** Every email ends in exactly one triage label, with a reason.
110	6. **Read-only and draft-only.** The system never sends mail and never touches the inbox.
111	7. **Synthetic is labeled.** The companies are real; the emails, brokers, positions, theses and estimates are not, and every screen says so.
112	
113	## Data flow
114	
115	Each email passes through the stages below, shown in the flow chart under "Overview". Code checks for repeats and Jev classifies every email. Two separate pathways follow: attention notes for emails that need a person, and the analysis agent for emails that bear on a thesis.
116	
117	### Stages
118	
119	| # | Stage | Input to output | How | Model |
120	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
121	| 1 | Parse | Raw email to parsed email | Read body, sender, subject line and other relevent information contained in the email json. Ignore labels. | None |
122	| 2 | Check for repeats | Parsed email to a redundancy record | Embed every email and compare it with every earlier email by cosine similarity. Subject similarity is a second signal. | Embedding model |
123	| 3 | Classify | Parsed email to a triage record | One Jev request per email with 14 typed questions, using the desk's relevance criteria. | Jev |
124	| 4 | Label and gate | Triage and redundancy records to a triage label and a gate decision | Thresholds and the redundancy flag, applied by code. | None |
125	| A | Write attention notes | Email flagged for human attention to an attention note | Summary, why it needs a person, the action asked for and any deadline. Quoted sections are checked by string match. | Small generative |
126	| 5 | Extract | Passed email to claims | Schema-constrained call. Each quoted section is checked by string match; failures are dropped and counted. | Analysis model |
127	| 6 | Analyze | Claims plus the candidate pillars, to suggestions or a no-change reason | The analysis agent calls a skill for each question: alter an existing thesis, or spawn a new one. | Analysis model |
128	| 7 | Validate | Suggestions to valid, or rejected with a reason | ID exists, quote matches, figure within bounds, new thesis is not a duplicate. | None |
129	| 8 | Merge and rank | Valid suggestions to one suggestion per thesis | Suggestions on the same pillar and stance merge, keeping every linked email and section. | None |
130	| 9 | Deliver | Labels, notes and suggestions to brief, alerts and audit view | Deterministic assembly. | None |
131	
132	Stage A runs alongside stages 5 to 8 and never touches the book. An email can take both pathways.
133	
134	After stage 9 the analyst accepts, edits or dismisses each suggestion. Only an accepted suggestion changes the book, through the change log.
135	
136	A verify agent sits outside the main line. On request it checks one suggestion against cached filings and the change log, and returns a cited verdict.
137	
138	The verify agent's tools are built from `tools/verify_agent.json`. Its filing search ranks paragraphs of the saved annual reports by embedding similarity, using the stage 2 model, and returns nothing when no report was saved. Its log search matches words in the session's change log.
139	
140	### Redundancy check
141	
142	Stage 2 runs before classification and keeps a cache of the day's subjects and vectors. For each email, in arrival order:
143	
144	1. **Embed the email.** Split the cleaned body into chunks that fit the embedding model's input limit, embed each chunk, and take the normalized mean as the email's vector.
145	2. **Compare content with every earlier email.** Take the highest cosine similarity and the email it belongs to.
146	3. **Compare subjects.** Normalize this email's subject and that earlier email's subject, and score their token-set similarity from 0 to 1.
147	4. **Flag.** The email is flagged as potentially redundant when content similarity reaches the content threshold, or reaches a lower threshold with a matching subject. It points to the most similar earlier email.
148	5. **Add the subject and vector to the cache,** whether or not the email was flagged.
149	
150	Four rules govern the check:
151	
152	- **The flag is a hint, not a verdict.** Stage 4 turns it into a redundant label only when the email's signal score is below the pass threshold.
153	- **A flagged email whose signal score clears the gate still passes.** The earlier email travels with it, and the analysis model keeps only claims the earlier email did not make. A repeat that carries one new insight is not lost.
154	- **Thresholds are fixed at 0.85 for content alone, or 0.75 with a subject score of 0.6 or more.** The corpus carries no `redundant_of` labels, so the check runs at run time with these values and is not swept.
155	- **The check finds same-day repeats only.** Each day is a separate set with its own cache, so `day_2` is never compared with `day_1`. An email that repeats consensus has no earlier email to match, so Jev's redundant label covers that case.
156	
157	### Classification with Jev
158	
159	Jev is used in stage 3 only. Each email goes to Jev once with 14 questions, which Jev answers in parallel as probabilities.
160	
161	Jev receives two things: the email (sender, sender address, subject and body) and the desk's relevance criteria. It never receives the book's positions, pillars or estimates, other emails, or the redundancy flag. Its answers therefore reflect what the desk has said is relevant, not what the desk currently believes.
162	
163	| Question | Type | Count |
164	| --- | --- | --- |
165	| Which triage label fits: thesis\_relevant, monitor, redundant, low\_value or irrelevant? | Choice | 1 |
166	| Is this company materially affected? Asked once per ticker. | Noul | 5 |
167	| Does it need direct human attention: a credible, valuable or time-sensitive request? | Bool | 1 |
168	| Does this topic label apply? Asked for macro, sector, government and other. | Noul | 4 |
169	| What kind of email is it: research, news, company release, invitation, newsletter or other? Display only. | Choice | 1 |
170	| Does it contain text that instructs an AI system? | Noul | 1 |
171	
172	The wording of all 14 questions lives in `instructions/jev_questions.md`. Eleven questions take their criteria from the criteria files described below. The email-kind question and the two safety questions have fixed wording and no criteria file.
173	
174	Stage 4 then sets the label and the gate, in this order:
175	
176	1. **Quarantine** if the prompt injection safety probability reaches the quarantine threshold. Nothing further runs on a quarantined email.
177	2. **Label.** The email takes Jev's most probable triage label. The one exception: a flagged repeat whose signal score is below the pass threshold is labeled redundant and points to the earlier email.
178	3. **Tickers and topics.** A company or topic is listed when its probability reaches its threshold.
179	4. **Human attention.** The flag is set when the attention probability reaches the attention threshold. Flagged emails take the attention pathway.
180	5. **Gate.** The email passes to the analysis model when its signal score reaches the pass threshold, or when it was truncated. The signal score is the combined probability of thesis\_relevant and monitor. Everything else stops, with its probabilities stored as the reason.
181	
182	Six rules govern classification:
183	
184	- **Jev's label is the label of record.** No later model relabels an email.
185	- **The gate reads the signal score, not the label.** An email labeled redundant, low\_value or irrelevant still passes when its signal score clears the gate, and any suggestion from it is marked "second look".
186	- **The pass threshold starts at 0.6.** The sweep under "Tuning" sets it and may move it either way.
187	- **A passes based on the first chunk.** Jev's limit is 32,000 tokens for the email plus the longest question, and a partial read is not grounds to stop an email.
188	- **Jev judges content, not presentation.** Its criteria repeat the corpus prompt's rule: never infer relevance from sender prestige, writing quality, format, subject line or length.
189	- **Order within the brief comes from Jev's scores.** Relevant emails without a suggestion are ordered by signal score, and attention notes by attention probability. Suggestions follow "Order and alerts".
190	
191	Every triage record keeps all 14 answers, and the audit view shows them.
192	
193	The reason on each result is one line that code composes from the probabilities and thresholds, such as "low\_value 0.62; signal score 0.11 is below 0.30". No model writes it.
194	
195	Four cases settle the remaining fields of a result:
196	
197	- **Quarantined.** The label is empty, the ticker and topic lists are empty, and the attention flag is false. The signal score is still stored, and the reason names the safety question and its probability.
198	- **Redundant by Jev alone.** `redundant_of` is empty and `decided_by` is `jev`.
199	- **Redundant by the check.** `decided_by` is `redundancy_check` only when the check changed the label. `redundant_of` is then the nearest earlier email.
200	- **Passed.** The reason names the signal score and the threshold it cleared, or says the email was truncated.
201	
202	A quarantined email's body reaches no model after stage 3 and no screen. Stage 5 leaves out an earlier email that was quarantined, and the Inbox shows only its sender and subject.
203	
204	### Relevance criteria
205	
206	The criteria Jev uses are plain text files, one per label. Anyone on the desk can read them, audit them and add a rule. The corpus labels never change: the files tune how Jev applies those labels, and every rule is measured against them.
207	
208	| Files in `criteria/` | Feed this Jev question |
209	| --- | --- |
210	| `thesis_relevant.md`, `monitor.md`, `redundant.md`, `low_value.md`, `irrelevant.md` | The five options of the triage question |
211	| `human_attention.md` | The human-attention question |
212	| `macro.md`, `sector.md`, `government.md`, `other.md` | The four topic questions |
213	| `affected_tickers.md` | The five company questions |
214	
215	Each file has a fixed definition and a list of rules. The rules below are illustrations.
216	
217	```text
218	# thesis_relevant
219	
220	## Definition
221	New, specific information that would support, challenge or change a reasonable
222	investment thesis on a target company: its earnings expectations, competitive
223	outlook, valuation or a trading decision.
224	
225	## Rules
226	- R1: Company guidance or a reported figure that differs from consensus counts.
227	- R2: First-hand information, such as a channel check, counts even when the
228	      email is short or informal.
229	- R3: News on a company outside the five counts only when the email states the
230	      read-through to one of them.
231	- R4: Sender prestige, length and formatting are not evidence of relevance.
232	```
233	
234	The files are used in five steps:
235	
236	1. **Load.** Code reads every file, checks its format and computes one version hash for the set.
237	2. **Compose.** Each label's definition and rules become the criteria for that option or question in the Jev request. Nothing else is added.
238	3. **Record.** Every triage record stores the version hash, so any label can be traced to the exact text that produced it.
239	4. **Tune.** Add or reword a rule, then run the criteria check. It reruns Jev on the tuning set, refits the thresholds, and prints scores before and after for each label, with the emails whose label changed. "Before" is the previous version's entry in the history file. The check appends a new entry and never writes the tuned thresholds.
240	5. **Keep or revert.** A rule stays when it passes the keep rule under "Tuning". The files' history in git is the audit trail.
241	
242	Five rules govern the files:
243	
244	- **Labels are fixed.** Label names and definitions come from the corpus prompt and are not edited. Tuning happens only under "Rules".
245	- **Rules describe kinds of information, never views.** Stances, pillars and estimates belong to the book. The load fails if a file names a pillar or driver ID.
246	- **Rules are tuned on the tuning set only.** Test-set scores are reported for the committed files and are never used to choose a rule.
247	- **Files stay short:** at most 12 rules a label, one sentence each. Jev makes snap judgments, and long criteria blur them.
248	- **The app shows the files as written.** The Criteria screen displays each file and its history, and the audit view links every email to the version in force.
249	
250	### Calling Jev
251	
252	Stage 3 can reach Jev by two routes. Step 0 runs one email through both and records the choice in `DECISIONS.md`.
253	
254	| Route | Call | Choose it when |
255	| --- | --- | --- |
256	| DSPy | `dspy.experimental.TypeSafe("jev-latest")` bound to one `dspy.Predict` signature with 14 top-level `Noul` and `Choice[...]` outputs | The criteria text can be set on the predictor's fields at run time. ReAnchor then fits the yes/no thresholds. |
257	| TypeSafe SDK | `TypeSafeClient().system_one(state=..., questions=...)` | The DSPy route cannot take criteria at run time. The code sweep then fits every threshold. |
258	
259	The SDK route maps directly onto the criteria files. This sketch follows the TypeSafe documentation; confirm the names against the pinned SDK.
260	
261	```python
262	from typesafe_sdk import Choice, Noul, TypeSafeClient
263	
264	TRIAGE = ["thesis_relevant", "monitor", "redundant", "low_value", "irrelevant"]
265	
266	def ask_jev(email: Email, criteria: CriteriaSet, wording: dict[str, str]):
267	    """wording maps a question ID to its sentence in instructions/jev_questions.md."""
268	
269	    def text(label: str) -> str:          # definition plus rules, as written
270	        c = criteria.labels[label]
271	        return "\n".join([c.definition, *(f"{r.id}: {r.text}" for r in c.rules)])
272	
273	    questions = {
274	        "triage": Choice(instructions=wording["triage"],
275	                         criteria={label: text(label) for label in TRIAGE}),
276	        "human_attention": Noul(instructions=wording["human_attention"],
277	                                criteria=text("human_attention")),
278	        "affects_NVDA": Noul(instructions=wording["affects_NVDA"],
279	                             criteria=text("affected_tickers")),
280	        # ...the other four tickers, topic_macro, topic_sector, topic_government,
281	        # topic_other, kind, possible_mnpi and instructs_ai: 14 in all
282	    }
283	    state = {"sender": email.sender, "sender_email": email.sender_email,
284	             "subject": email.subject, "body": email.body}
285	    with TypeSafeClient() as client:
286	        answers = client.system_one(state=state, questions=questions).answers
287	    return answers    # answers["triage"].probabilities, answers["human_attention"].noul
288	```
289	
290	Eight facts the build depends on:
291	
292	- **Read first.** The DSPy 3.4.0 release notes and the TypeSafe Primitives page, both under "Sources".
293	- **Pins.** `dspy[typesafe]==3.4.0`, `typesafe-sdk>=0.6.0,<1.0.0`, and Pydantic 2.11 or later.
294	- **Answers.** The SDK returns `probabilities` for a Choice and `noul`, the probability of yes, for a Noul. DSPy exposes them as `.probabilities` and `.probability`.
295	- **Criteria.** A Choice takes a map from option to text. A Noul takes one optional text that says what yes and no mean. Each text is a file's definition and rules, as written.
296	- **One file, five questions.** `affected_tickers.md` supplies the criteria for all five company questions. The question wording names the company.
297	- **Thresholds stay local.** Jev returns probabilities and code applies the thresholds. In DSPy a threshold sits on the predictor, as in `predictor.fields["human_attention"] = {"threshold": 0.3}`.
298	- **ReAnchor.** `ReAnchor(metric=...).compile(program, trainset=fit, valset=validation)` returns a tuned copy and needs caching on.
299	- **Trimming.** When the email plus the longest question would exceed 32,000 tokens, stage 3 keeps the start of the body and sets `truncated`. Count four characters as one token unless the SDK offers a counter.
300	
301	### Attention pathway
302	
303	Emails that Jev flags for human attention take a separate pathway from the thesis analysis. A small generative model writes an attention note, so the analyst can act without reading the whole email.
304	
305	Each note holds:
306	
307	- a summary of the email in two sentences;
308	- the reason it needs a person, in one or two sentences;
309	- the action asked for, such as reply, attend or decide;
310	- the deadline, if the email states one;
311	- the quoted sections that support the note.
312	
313	Three rules govern the pathway:
314	
315	- **Jev alone decides which emails are flagged.** The note explains the flag and cannot remove it.
316	- **A note describes and explains.** It never recommends an investment action and never touches the book.
317	- **Every quoted section is checked against the email by code.**
318	
319	### Analysis agent
320	
321	Stage 6 is an analysis agent with a narrow job: say how new information may alter an existing thesis, or whether it should spawn a new one. It does nothing else. Each job is a separate skill the agent calls.
322	
323	| Skill | Question it answers | What it is given | What it returns |
324	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
325	| Alter an existing thesis | Does this information support or contradict a pillar, or meet its "wrong if" test? | The claims, and the candidate pillars with their stance and linked drivers | A suggestion on one pillar: stance, strength, whether the test is met, and any figure the email states for a linked assumption |
326	| Spawn a new thesis | Does this information point to a thesis the book does not hold? | The claims, one ticker, and the statements of that company's pillars | A candidate pillar: statement, what would prove it wrong, and linked drivers |
327	
328	Five rules govern the agent:
329	
330	- **Each skill is its own prompt file and DSPy module.** Adding a skill means adding a file and registering it; the agent's own prompt does not grow.
331	- **The agent chooses which skills to call for each email,** with at most three calls.
332	- **The new-thesis skill is for information that fits no existing pillar.** Code rejects a candidate that restates one.
333	- **Skills recommend and never decide.** Every output is a suggestion for the analyst.
334	- **No skill proposes a number, a trade or a position size.** A figure appears only when the email states it.
335	
336	Five mechanics make the agent buildable:
337	
338	- **Code picks the candidate pillars.** They are every pillar of each company in the claims' `tickers`, plus the pillars the links file ties to those companies. The agent passes claim IDs only, and the new-thesis skill takes one ticker a call.
339	- **The existing-thesis skill sees stance, pillars and linked drivers.** Each driver shows its label, unit, desk value and consensus. A skill never sees size or conviction, and never copies a book value into its output. The new-thesis skill sees one company's pillar statements and its drivers' IDs, labels and units.
340	- **A skill sees Jev's label for each email.** This is the pipeline's own label from stage 4, never the corpus label.
341	- **The agent is a tool loop.** Its tools are built from `tools/analysis_agent.json`: name, description and input schema, with `returns` appended to the description. Each tool runs one skill module. The agent itself is given the claims and the statements of the candidate pillars.
342	- **Code collects the output.** Suggestions come from the skills' results, parsed with the draft contracts, never from the agent's final text. The no-change reason is the last skill's own reason, and the agent's final text is used only when no skill was called.
343	
344	### Tuning
345	
346	- **Stages 3, A, 5 and 6 are DSPy modules.** Stage 3 binds the TypeSafe backend; the others bind generative models.
347	- **A code sweep fits the gate.** It sets the pass threshold on the fit split, picking the highest value that still passes every thesis\_relevant email and at least 95% of monitor emails. The three redundancy thresholds are not swept: the corpus has no `redundant_of` labels to score them against.
348	- **ReAnchor fits the yes/no thresholds.** It sets the attention, ticker and topic thresholds for the best F1 on the fit split. ReAnchor is experimental; if it proves unreliable, the same code sweep replaces it.
349	- **The quarantine threshold is not tuned.** The corpus holds no positive examples, so it stays at its starting value and is covered by test fixtures.
350	- **Criteria rules are tuned by hand, in text.** Add a rule, run the criteria check, and apply the keep rule below.
351	- **Small samples are noisy.** The tuning set holds about 15 thesis\_relevant emails, so a change of one email is not evidence. The keep rule: a rule stays only when it fixes at least two fit-split emails, breaks none that were right, and signal accuracy on the validation split does not fall.
352	- **Prompt optimization is optional.** GEPA or MIPROv2 can tune the skill prompts; this is the first thing to cut.
353	- **Tuned settings are files.** Each is saved as JSON and loaded at run time, so thresholds stay readable and editable.
354	- **The 600 test emails in `day_1` and `day_2` are never used for tuning.**

382	### How to construct it
383	
384	- **Each stage is a function from files to files.** Stage N reads the JSON that earlier stages wrote and writes its own. Any stage reruns alone. "Stage files" lists every file and its contract.
385	- **Emails are processed in arrival order.** The day cache makes stage 2 depend on what came before.
386	- **The parsed body is the text of record.** Every model reads it, every quote is checked against it after each run of whitespace is collapsed to one space, and the app highlights quotes in it. The Inbox shows the raw email.
387	- **Every model call and every embedding is cached on disk,** keyed by program version, criteria version and input hash. Reruns cost nothing and the demo is deterministic.
388	- **The cache is committed.** A clean clone reruns the pipeline without spending tokens. Only a cache miss needs the keys.
389	- **No test calls a live model.** Each module takes its client as an argument, and tests pass a fake client or replay the cache.
390	- **The live route calls the same stage functions** on one email, against the day cache and the visitor's session state.
391	- **Each skill sees only what it needs:** the claims, and the candidate pillars with their stance and linked drivers.
392	- **Read-throughs come from a links file,** not the model's memory. When a claim tags one company, linked pillars on other companies are added to the candidates.
393	- **Code fills the book's current value and consensus** wherever a suggestion shows a linked assumption. The model never restates them.
394	
395	### Monitoring: token use and latency
396	
397	Every run records how many tokens each email cost and how long each stage took, so the cost and speed of processing a day are visible and comparable across runs.
398	
399	1. **Wrap every client.** `monitoring.py` wraps each model client and the embedder that a module receives as its argument. Each call appends one `CallRecord`: the stage, email ID, model ID, input and output tokens, whether it was a cache hit, and wall-clock latency. Modules do not time themselves.
400	2. **Time every stage.** `pipeline/run.py` times each stage's `process(...)` call per email and its `run(...)` call per set, and appends a `StageTiming`.
401	3. **Write two files per set.** `usage.json` holds every `CallRecord` and `StageTiming` of the run. `metrics.json` holds the `UsageReport` that code computes from them.
402	4. **Print a summary.** At the end of a run, `run.py` prints tokens and latency per stage, and totals for the set.
403	
404	Five rules govern monitoring:
405	
406	- **Counts come from the provider.** Token counts are read from each response's usage fields. Where a provider reports none, as Jev may not, code estimates them at four characters per token and marks the record `estimated`.
407	- **Cache hits are kept apart.** A cache hit records the original call's tokens with `cache_hit` true and its own lookup latency. The report shows tokens spent on this run (misses only) separately from tokens the run would have cost uncached.
408	- **No content is logged.** Records hold IDs, counts and times only. They never hold prompt text, email text or keys.
409	- **Fakes report too.** A fake client reports fixed token counts, so tests check aggregation without a live model.
410	- **Latency is wall-clock, per email and per stage,** with p50, p95 and max computed by code. Stages that run per set, such as redundancy, are also timed per email.
411	
412	The Monitor screen shows the latest `metrics.json` for the set, and the Live screen shows tokens and latency beside each stage of its trace.

430	- **One inbox, many books.** Editing the seed files and rerunning stages 6 to 9 gives a different brief from the same emails.
431	- **Two things are measured separately.** Labels are scored against the corpus. Suggestions are reviewed by hand, because no label knows the book.

560	
561	Each entry records the book item, the value before and after, the quoted sections that supported the change, and a timestamp. An entry is written only when the analyst accepts a suggestion, and entries are held on the server for each visitor session. Reset clears the session log, and undo appends a reversing entry.

934	### Stage files
935	
936	Each stage file is a JSON list of one contract, except the brief and the eval report, which are single objects. These files are the only interfaces between stages, and between work packages.
937	
938	| File in `data/out/<set>/` | Contract | Written by | Read by |
939	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
940	| `parsed.json` | `Email`, with the cleaned body | 1 Parse | Stages 2, 3, A, 5 and 7; the app |
941	| `vectors.npy` | One row per email, in the order of `parsed.json` | 2 Check for repeats | The live route |
942	| `redundancy.json` | `RedundancyRecord` | 2 Check for repeats | Stages 4 and 5; the app |
943	| `triage.json` | `TriageRecord` | 3 Classify | Stage 4; evals; the app |
944	| `results.json` | `EmailResult` | 4 Label and gate | Stages A and 5 to 9; evals; the app |
945	| `notes.json` | `AttentionNote` | A Write attention notes | Stage 9; the app |
946	| `claims.json` | `Claim` | 5 Extract | Stages 6 and 7; the app |
947	| `analysis.json` | `AnalysisRecord` | 6 Analyze | Stage 9; the app |
948	| `suggestions_raw.json` | `Suggestion`, all with status open | 6 Analyze | Stage 7 |
949	| `suggestions_checked.json` | `Suggestion`, open or rejected with a reason | 7 Validate | Stage 8; evals; the app's audit view |
950	| `suggestions.json` | `Suggestion`, merged and ordered | 8 Merge and rank | Stage 9; the app |
951	| `brief.json` | `Brief` | 9 Deliver | The app |
952	| `eval.json` | `EvalReport` | The eval script | The app |
953	| `usage.json` | `CallRecord` and `StageTiming`, as two lists under `calls` and `timings` | `pipeline/run.py`, through the monitoring wrappers | `metrics.json`; the app |
954	| `metrics.json` | `UsageReport` | `pipeline/run.py` | The app's Monitor screen |

957	
958	Five rules cover what the table leaves out:
959	
960	- **Stage modules share one interface.** Each `pipeline/<stage>.py` exposes `run(in_dir, out_dir, ctx)` for a whole set and `process(...)` for one email. `ctx` is a `RunContext` (`pipeline/context.py`) holding the clients, recorder, cache, criteria and thresholds; tests pass fakes through it. The stage names are parse, redundancy, classify, gate, attention, extract, analyze, validate, merge and deliver. Package 0 commits a typed stub of all ten.
961	- **Each set's outputs are kept apart.** The sets are `day_1`, `day_2` and `tuning`, named after their folders in `data/corpus/`. A run on a set writes its stage files to `data/out/<set>/`. The app reads the directory named in `TRIAGE_DATA_DIR`, which defaults to `data/out/day_1`; the deployed app uses the default once the final run exists, and the fixtures until then.
962	- **Tuned thresholds override starting values.** Stage 4 reads `tuned/thresholds.json` when it exists and `thresholds.py` otherwise. Stage 2 always uses the fixed values in `thresholds.py`.
963	- **Code assigns every ID.** A claim is `<email_id>.c<n>` and a raw suggestion is `<email_id>.s<n>`. After merging, a suggestion is `<pillar_id>.<stance>` or `<ticker>.new<n>`. A model never writes an ID of its own.
964	- **Session state is not a stage file.** The change log, each suggestion's accepted or dismissed status, and conviction reviews live in the visitor's session. Code raises a conviction review when an accepted entry crosses the threshold.
965	
966	## Labels and suggestions
967	
968	Every email gets one triage label in stage 4. Emails flagged for attention get a note, and emails that pass the gate can produce thesis suggestions. A suggestion is a recommendation: no model makes an investment decision, and nothing changes the book until the analyst accepts.
969	
970	### What each label leads to
971	
972	| Label or flag | Set by | What happens next | Usually appears in |
973	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
974	| thesis\_relevant | Jev | Goes to the analysis agent when it passes the gate, which it normally does. | Brief, with any suggestions |
975	| monitor | Jev | The same. Its suggestions are capped at strength 1. | Brief, under "worth watching" |
976	| redundant | Jev, or the redundancy check with a pointer to the earlier email | Stops, unless its signal score clears the gate. | Audit view, listed under the earlier email |
977	| low\_value | Jev | Stops, unless its signal score clears the gate. | Audit view |
978	| irrelevant | Jev | Stops, unless its signal score clears the gate. | Audit view |
979	| human\_attention | Jev | Takes the attention pathway and gets a note. | Brief, under "needs your attention" |
980	| Quarantine | Jev's two safety questions | Held unsummarized. | Quarantine list on the audit screen |
981	
982	"Where each email appears" governs when an email fits more than one row.
983	
984	### Kinds of suggestion
985	
986	| Kind | Comes from | Raised when | What the analyst is shown |
987	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
988	| Change to an existing thesis | The existing-thesis skill | A claim supports or contradicts a pillar, or meets its "wrong if" test. | The pillar, the stance, a strength from 1 to 3, whether the test is met, and any stated figure beside the linked assumption. |
989	| New thesis | The new-thesis skill | Relevant information fits no existing pillar. | A candidate pillar: statement, what would prove it wrong, and linked drivers. |
990	| Conviction review | Code | Accepted contradicting evidence on one pillar reaches a net strength of 4. | A prompt to review conviction, with the evidence behind it. |
991	
992	Every suggestion carries a one-sentence rationale and its linked emails, each opened at the quoted sections that support it. No suggestion proposes a number of its own, a trade or a position size.
993	
994	### What the analyst can do
995	
996	- **Accept.** For an existing thesis, the evidence is logged against the pillar. For a new thesis, the pillar is added to the book.
997	- **Update a linked assumption.** Where a suggestion shows a stated figure, the analyst can change the driver, and the app recomputes EPS and target price.
998	- **Edit.** Change the strength or the wording of a new pillar, then accept.
999	- **Dismiss.** The suggestion closes and stays visible in the company's history.
1000	- **Set conviction.** On a conviction review, the analyst picks a conviction from 1 to 5 or dismisses the review. The app never proposes the value.
1001	- **Verify.** An agent checks the claim against cached filings and returns a cited verdict.
1002	
1003	### Validation in stage 7
1004	
1005	- **Unknown item:** a claim ID is not one of the email's claims, a pillar ID is outside the candidate set recomputed from those claims' tickers, a new thesis names a ticker outside them, or a new pillar names a driver of another company. Reject.
1006	- **Quote mismatch:** a section is not found verbatim after whitespace normalization. Reject.
1007	- **Duplicate thesis:** a new-thesis candidate's statement reaches the duplicate threshold against an existing pillar, using the stage 2 embedding model. Reject.
1008	- **Monitor only:** every linked email is labeled monitor. Set strength to 1, and reject a new-thesis candidate.
1009	- **Out of bounds:** a stated figure falls outside the driver's bounds, or names a driver the pillar is not linked to. Keep the suggestion and drop the figure.
1010	- **Wrong period:** the claim's period is missing, or is not exactly the model's fiscal year, such as FY2027. Keep the suggestion and drop the figure.
1011	- **Second look:** no linked email is labeled thesis\_relevant or monitor. Keep the suggestion and mark it "second look".
1012	
1013	### Merging in stage 8
1014	
1015	Suggestions on the same pillar and stance merge into one, which lists every linked email. Four rules settle the merged record:
1016	
1017	- **Strongest wins.** Strength is the highest among them, `wrong_if_met` is true if any was, and the rationale is the strongest one's.
1018	- **Assumptions are pooled,** one entry per driver and stated value.
1019	- **Opposite stances stay apart.** Two stances on one pillar remain two suggestions. The app shows them together as one card, and neither is preselected.
1020	- **Similar candidates merge.** New-thesis candidates for one company merge when their statements reach the merge threshold. The first statement is kept.
1021	
1022	After merging, code recomputes the second-look mark and the worth-watching placement from the merged emails.
1023	
1024	### Order and alerts
1025	
1026	Suggestions on existing pillars are ordered by position size, then strength, then the signal score of their strongest email. New-thesis candidates are ordered by position size, then signal score.
1027	
1028	An item alerts in three cases: a "wrong if" test is met on a position of 150 basis points or more, a conviction review is triggered, or a human-attention probability reaches 0.8. The budget is three a day; overflow stays in the brief.
1029	
1030	Met tests come first, by position size, then attention items by probability. A conviction review is raised in the session, is shown first and counts toward the three. Alerts appear as a banner at the top of the Brief.
1031	
1032	### Where each email appears
1033	
1034	| Email | Appears in |
1035	| --- | --- |
1036	| Quarantined | The quarantine list, by sender and subject only |
1037	| Flagged for human attention | "Needs your attention", whatever else applies to it |
1038	| Passed, with a valid suggestion | That suggestion's card: thesis changes, new thesis candidates, or "worth watching" when every linked email is labeled monitor |
1039	| Passed, labeled thesis\_relevant or monitor, with no valid suggestion | "Relevant with no link to your book", with the no-change reason |
1040	| Passed, with any other label and no valid suggestion | The audit view, with the no-change reason |
1041	| Stopped | The audit view, with its reason |
1042	
1043	A second-look suggestion stays in its own list, thesis changes or new thesis candidates, and is marked. A rejected suggestion appears only in the audit view, under its email, with the reject reason.
1044	
1045	Two no-change reasons are written by code. When every suggestion from an email was rejected, the reason reads "all suggestions rejected in validation". When stage 5 found no claims, it reads "no claims extracted".

1047	## Corpus: two test days of 300 emails, plus a tuning set
1048	
1049	The corpus is whatever the corpus prompt in `docs/corpus_documentation/synthetic_data_prompt.md` produces. That prompt is the specification for the emails, and the pipeline adapts to its output. It contains no book: labels are written for an informed generalist who holds no position. The test corpus is two days of 300 emails each: `day_1` (Tuesday, Oct 13, 2026; `synthetic_000001` to `synthetic_000300`) and `day_2` (Wednesday, Oct 14, 2026; `synthetic_000301` to `synthetic_000600`). Each day is a separate set with its own run, brief and eval report. The tuning set is a separate run of the same prompt, still being generated.
1050	
1051	### File format
1052	
1053	Each set is one JSONL file, `data/corpus/<set>/emails.jsonl`, with one object per email and 14 fields. An `email_plan.jsonl` beside it holds the label plan the emails were written against. Only the loader and evals read it.
1054	
1055	| Field | Role | Notes |
1056	| --- | --- | --- |
1057	| email\_id | Input | For example synthetic\_000001 |
1058	| sender | Input | Free text naming a fictional person and organization |
1059	| sender\_email | Input |  |
1060	| subject | Input |  |
1061	| body | Input | No length limit; may hold several items or forwarded material |
1062	| triage | Label | One of the five primary labels |
1063	| additional\_labels | Label | Any of macro, sector, government, other; may also hold human\_attention |
1064	| affected\_tickers | Label | Any of the five tickers; empty when none is meaningfully affected |
1065	| human\_attention | Label | True or false |
1066	| reason | Label | The generator's justification; never shown to a model |
1067	| email\_type | Generation label | Format, such as sell\_side\_research or meeting\_request; never shown to a model |
1068	| systemic | Generation label | True when one development affects all five targets; never shown to a model |
1069	| angle | Generation label | How the email earns its label; never shown to a model |
1070	| day | Generation label | 1 or 2; never shown to a model |
1071	
1072	The corpus has no `received_at` and no `redundant_of`. The loader assigns `received_at` in file order across the day's trading window. Redundancy is computed only at run time by stage 2, and no label says which earlier email a repeat copies.
1073	
1074	### Label targets set by the prompt
1075	
1076	| Label | Share | Emails per 300 |
1077	| --- | --- | --- |
1078	| thesis\_relevant | 10% | 30 |
1079	| monitor | 15% | 45 |
1080	| redundant | 10% | 30 |
1081	| low\_value | 35% | 105 |
1082	| irrelevant | 30% | 90 |
1083	| **Total** | **100%** | **300** |
1084	
1085	The prompt sets further targets, and five are checked. The loader reports the first, third and fourth. The eval script reports the second after stage 3, from Jev's email kind, under the key meetings\_share. The fifth uses a name-and-ticker match and is approximate.
1086	
1087	- human\_attention is true on 15 to 25 emails.
1088	- Meeting requests, newsletters and event announcements make up at least 60 emails.
1089	- Macro, sector or government labels appear on 25 to 35 emails.
1090	- Each ticker appears at about the same rate among thesis\_relevant emails, about six each.
1091	- No more than 15% of low\_value and irrelevant emails name a target company directly.
1092	
1093	### The loader
1094	
1095	The loader does five things, in order:
1096	
1097	1. Splits each row into an Email and an EmailLabel.
1098	2. Normalizes label spellings, using the table below. Version 3 of the prompt removes these inconsistencies; the table stays as a safety net.
1099	3. Checks that IDs increase in file order, and assigns each row a `received_at` in that order within its day.
1100	4. Validates every row against the schema and lists failures for hand fixing.
1101	5. Prints a distribution report against the prompt's targets.
1102	
1103	| Found in a row | What the loader does |
1104	| --- | --- |
1105	| `relevent` or `relevant` as the triage value | Reads it as thesis\_relevant. |
1106	| `macro_government` in additional\_labels | Splits it into macro and government. |
1107	| `human_attention` as the triage value or inside additional\_labels | Sets the flag to true. If no primary label remains, lists the row for hand fixing. |
1108	| A lower-case ticker, or GOOG | Upper-cases it and maps GOOG to GOOGL. |
1109	| Any other label or ticker | Drops it and logs a warning. |
1110	| Two rows with the same subject and body | Keeps the first and reports the pair. |
1111	
1112	### Hard negatives are the test
1113	
1114	The prompt plants noise that looks like signal. The pipeline must not surface any of these:
1115	
1116	- Excellent research on companies with no read-through to the five.
1117	- Sophisticated analysis of a target company that only repeats consensus.
1118	- Detailed, data-heavy reports with no thesis-changing conclusion.
1119	- Routine analyst meetings that offer no differentiated access.
1120	- Prestigious conference invitations that are irrelevant to the desk.
1121	- Credible macro commentary with no plausible effect on the five.
1122	- Important-looking legal or government announcements with little real relevance.
1123	- Useful analysis mixed with promotional or irrelevant material.
1124	
1125	It must also catch the reverse: an understated email that holds a single material insight.
1126	
1127	### What the labels cannot check
1128	
1129	- **Impact on the book.** The corpus has no book, so no label says which pillar or driver an email bears on. Suggestions are reviewed by hand.
1130	- **Whether the labels are right.** One generator wrote the emails and the labels, so the labels are its judgment of general relevance, not an analyst's.
1131	- **Safety handling.** The prompt forbids confidential information and plants no instructions aimed at an AI, so quarantine is tested by two fixtures in the test suite, not by the corpus.
1132	
1133	### Tuning set
1134	
1135	- **Source:** a separate run of the same prompt into `data/corpus/tuning/`, planned at 100 emails (`synthetic_000601` onward, Thursday, Oct 15, 2026). It is being generated outside this build; the agent never generates or edits it.
1136	- **Handling:** loaded and normalized exactly like the test days.
1137	- **Separation:** checked against both test days by subject and body hash; overlaps are removed.
1138	- **Internal split:** two-thirds to fit and one-third to validate, stratified by triage label with a fixed seed. The split is made in `corpus.py`.
1139	
1140	Until `data/corpus/tuning/emails.jsonl` exists, tuning and the criteria check are reported as pending and the pipeline runs at starting values.

1142	## Stack and repo layout
1143	
1144	The whole application is Python, including the UI. Pages are rendered on the server, so there is no TypeScript and no front-end build step.
1145	
1146	| Layer | Default | Why |
1147	| --- | --- | --- |
1148	| Language | Python 3.14 | One codebase and one set of models |
1149	| Packaging | uv with a lock file | The same environment for the agent and the host |
1150	| Contracts | Pydantic 2.11 or later | Runtime validation of model output; DSPy 3.4 requires it |
1151	| Pipeline framework | DSPy 3.4 with its TypeSafe extra | Signatures, a model per stage, and ReAnchor |
1152	| Classifier | Jev through the TypeSafe SDK, pinned to jev-1.13.0 | Tuned thresholds must not move with a new release |
1153	| Criteria | Plain text files in the repo, one per label, loaded into the Jev questions at run time | Anyone can read, diff and extend them; git history is the audit trail |
1154	| Subject matching | Token-set similarity, for example with rapidfuzz | A second signal beside content similarity; fast and local |
1155	| Content similarity | A Hugging Face embedding model, pulled from the Hub with `huggingface-hub` and run locally with `sentence-transformers` (default `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5`), in `triage_app/embed.py`; long emails chunked to its input limit; cosine similarity in NumPy | Every email is embedded; no vector database, and no API key for embeddings |
1156	| Model access | Every generative call goes through OpenRouter, in `triage_app/llm.py`; Jev keeps its own TypeSafe client | One key and one client for every generative model |

1158	| Attention notes model | Claude Haiku 4.5 (OpenRouter `anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5`) | Short summaries do not need the larger model |
1159	| Skills | One prompt file and one DSPy module per skill, registered with the analysis agent | A new investment question is a new file, not a longer prompt |
1160	| Web | FastAPI with Jinja templates and HTMX | Server-rendered pages; one process to deploy |
1161	| Storage | JSON and text files in the repo; accepted changes in server memory, keyed by a session cookie | No database; every visitor starts clean, and a restart clears sessions |
1162	| Cache | Model calls cached in development; pipeline output and the test day's vectors committed | The deployed app never reruns the corpus, and the live route can compare a new email with the day |
1163	| Tests | pytest on the loader, redundancy check, gate, compute, fold, validate and merge | Pure functions are cheap to test |
1164	| Deploy | One container on any host that runs Python; the image includes the embedding model | Pages and the live route ship together |
1165	| Secrets | OpenRouter key and TypeSafe key, read from OPENROUTER\_API\_KEY and TYPESAFE\_API\_KEY in `.env`, server-side only. Other keys in `.env` are unused | Never sent to the browser |

1310	### Working rules for the coding agent
1311	
1312	- Read `SPEC.md` whole before step 0.
1313	- Commit after each step, and keep the full session transcript. The transcript is a submission deliverable.
1314	- Where this spec is silent or contradicts itself, follow the design rules, choose the simpler option and record the choice in `DECISIONS.md`.
1315	- Commit every file a generation prompt produces as a draft, and list it in `REVIEW.md`. Do not tune on a generated file that has not been listed.
1316	- Pin the DSPy and TypeSafe SDK versions. The Jev integration is experimental and has no generative fallback.
1317	- If the DSPy backend cannot take criteria text at run time, call the TypeSafe SDK directly for stage 3 and keep everything else unchanged.
1318	- Send all 14 questions in one Jev request per email, never one request per question.
1319	- Give Jev the email and the relevance criteria only: no book, no redundancy flag and no other emails.
1320	- Keep views out of the criteria files, and never change a label's name or definition. Add rules beneath it.
1321	- Keep each skill in its own prompt file and module. The analysis agent calls skills; it does not absorb them.
1322	- Process emails in arrival order, so the day cache holds only earlier emails.
1323	- No pipeline stage passes a corpus label, including its reason, to a model. Only the loader, eval and tuning code read EmailLabel. Jev's own label from stage 4 is pipeline output and may be shown to a skill.
1324	- Tune only on the tuning set, and report scores only on the test days, `day_1` and `day_2`.
1325	- Do not edit the corpus prompt or the emails to make a score pass. Report the miss.
1326	- Never commit, print or log an API key. Commit `.env.example`, never `.env`.

1340	| 6 | Analysis | The extract, analysis agent, skill and verify modules with their tool functions; `pipeline/extract.py`, `analyze.py`, `validate.py`, `merge.py` | `parsed.json`, `results.json`, `redundancy.json`, the seed files, `skills/`, `instructions/` and `tools/`, then `claims.json`, `analysis.json` and the three suggestion files | Analysis agent; Labels and suggestions; Read-through links; Data contracts | With fake clients, each validation rule and each merge rule has a test, and every output validates. |
1341	| 7 | State and app | `state/apply.py`, `pipeline/deliver.py`, `web/` | Every stage file and the seed files, then `brief.json`, the pages and the session log | State; Labels and suggestions; Screens; Routes; Data contracts; Stage files; Starting values; the live-route rules under "Stack and repo layout" | Build step 5 passes on the fixtures. Every route under "Routes" answers, with a fake standing in for any module another package owns. Brief items plus audit items account for every fixture email. |
1342	| 8 | Evals and tuning | `evals/` | The stage files and `labels.jsonl`, then `thresholds.json`, `eval.json`, `criteria_history.json` and the review sheets | Tuning; Starting values; Evaluation and guardrails; Stage files | The eval, tuning and criteria-check commands run on the fixtures, with a fake classifier, and write valid files. |
1343	| 9 | Review, in a fresh context | Nothing; it is read-only | The repo and this spec, then a findings report | Design rules; Guardrails; Working rules | Every check in the last rule below passes, or the failure is reported. |
1344	| L | Integration, by the lead | `Dockerfile`, `.env.example`, `DECISIONS.md`, `REVIEW.md`, `data/cache/`, `data/out/`, `data/live_presets/`, `tuned/`, `transcripts/` | The merged packages and both corpora, then the committed outputs and the deployed app | Build order; Where a person is needed; Commands | Build steps 1 to 7 pass on the real sets. |
1345	
1346	Packages 1 to 8 can start together once package 0 is merged, because each builds and tests against the fixtures and stubs. Packages 4 and 6 use stub wording until the drafts from package 1 land.
1347	
1348	The lead then integrates in stage order. Once the tuning set exists, it runs the pipeline on it and produces the tuning-set report that build step 3 names. It then tunes, makes the final run on `day_1` and `day_2`, and deploys.
1349	
1350	Nine rules govern the hand-off:
1351	
1352	- **Contracts freeze first.** Only the lead edits `schema.py`, `config.py` and `thresholds.py`. A subagent that needs a contract changed stops and asks.
1353	- **One owner per file.** A package edits only the files it owns and adds tests only for them. A subagent returns lines for `REVIEW.md` and `DECISIONS.md` in its report; the lead writes them.
1354	- **Fixtures stand in for upstream stages.** `tests/fixtures/` holds ten hand-written emails and a valid example of every stage file, so no package waits for another to run. The ten include two quarantine cases, a same-day repeat with its earlier email, an attention email and a second-look case.
1355	- **A brief stands alone.** A subagent starts with no memory of the lead's session. Its brief names the package row, the spec sections to read, the contracts it uses, the done-when test and the working rules.
1356	- **A report is evidence.** A subagent returns the files it changed, the test command with its output, any choice for `DECISIONS.md`, and anything left undone. The lead reruns the test before merging.
1357	- **Labels stay with two packages.** Fixture labels sit in `tests/fixtures/labels.jsonl`. Only the loader in package 2 and the evals in package 8 read `EmailLabel`, and no brief includes a test-set label.
1358	- **Only the lead runs a full corpus.** Subagents call live models on fixtures only, through the cache. This keeps cost bounded and makes the committed outputs come from one run.
1359	- **Every transcript is kept.** Each subagent's brief, transcript and report go in `transcripts/`. They are part of the submission's record of AI interactions.
1360	- **Review is independent.** Package 9 gets the repo and this spec, not the lead's summary. It checks that no corpus label reaches a prompt, the Jev request holds only the email and criteria, every quote matches its email, no tool writes or sends, a quarantined body reaches no later model or screen, every screen is marked synthetic, and the test set was never used for tuning.
1361	
1362	## Evaluation and guardrails
1363	
1364	The eval script compares pipeline output with the labels and writes the scores the eval page shows. Scores are reported on the test days only, one `eval.json` per day, and the targets are proposals.
1365	
1366	| Measure | Key in `eval.json` | Definition | Target |
1367	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
1368	| Gate recall | `gate_recall` | Emails the corpus labels thesis\_relevant that pass the gate. | 100% |
1369	| Monitor recall at the gate | `monitor_gate_recall` | Emails the corpus labels monitor that pass the gate. | 95% or better |
1370	| Gate reduction | `gate_reduction` | Share of emails stopped before the analysis model. | Reported, not targeted |
1371	| Signal accuracy | `signal_accuracy` | Label correct on three classes: signal (thesis\_relevant or monitor), redundant, and noise (low\_value or irrelevant). | 85% or better |
1372	| Triage accuracy | `triage_accuracy` | Label equals the corpus label exactly, on all five. | Reported, with a confusion table |
1373	| Ticker tagging | `ticker_f1` | Micro-averaged F1 on affected\_tickers. | 0.90 or better |
1374	| Human attention | `attention_precision`, `attention_recall` | Precision and recall on the flag. | Recall 90% or better; precision 80% or better |
1375	| Topic labels | `topic_f1` | Micro-averaged F1 on macro, sector, government and other. | Reported |
1376	| Repeat detection | `repeat_flagged`, `repeat_precision` | Count of emails the check flags, and the share of flagged emails the corpus labels redundant. The corpus has no `redundant_of`, so recall and match to the right earlier email are not measured. | Reported |
1377	| Stray suggestions | `stray_suggestions` | Count of suggestions whose only linked emails are labeled redundant, low\_value or irrelevant. | Reported; each one reviewed |
1378	| Quote faithfulness | `quote_faithfulness` | Quoted sections that match the source exactly, in notes and suggestions. | 100%, enforced by code |
1379	| Attention note review | `note_review` | Hand review of every note: summary accurate, reason and action stated. | 90% or better |
1380	| Suggestion review | `suggestion_review` | Hand review of every suggestion: right pillar, right stance, sections support it. | 90% or better |
1381	| New-thesis review | `new_thesis_review` | Hand review of every candidate: new to the book and supported by its sections. | Reported |
1382	
1383	A quarantined email counts as a miss on every label measure. Each review sheet has one row per item: its ID, its kind, a yes-or-no column for each check, and a comment. Checks that do not apply to a kind stay blank. A row passes when every applicable check is yes, and each review key is the share of passing rows. The person commits the filled sheets and the eval script reads them; until then the three review keys are empty.
1384	
1385	Label scores are reported for the criteria files as committed. The corpus labels are fixed, and rules are tuned on the tuning set only.
1386	
1387	The labels come from the same generator as the emails, so these scores show internal consistency, not performance on real mail.
1388	
1389	The three hand reviews are done by a person, not by the coding agent. The agent writes one review sheet for notes and one for suggestions, and the eval page shows their results once they are filled in.
1390	
1391	### Guardrails
1392	
1393	- **No model makes an investment decision.** Models recommend; suggestions concern theses, never trades, position sizes or numbers of the model's own.
1394	- **Nothing changes the book without the analyst.** Suggestions pass stage 7 before they are shown, and only an accepted suggestion is logged.
1395	- **Classification stays free of the desk's views.** Jev gets the email and the relevance criteria, and the criteria hold no stances, pillars or estimates.
1396	- **Email text is data.** It is delimited in every prompt and models return schema-bound output only. No tool can write, send or browse, so text in an email cannot cause an action.
1397	- **Read-only on mail.** The system never sends mail and never touches the inbox.
1398	- **Possible inside information is quarantined,** not summarized.
1399	- **Synthetic content is labeled** on every screen.
1400	- **Only synthetic mail goes to Jev and the generative models.** Sending real fund email to any vendor needs a compliance and data-processing review first.
1401	- **API keys stay server-side,** and the live route is rate-limited.
1402	
1403	## Beyond the prototype
1404	
1405	With more time, the claim ledger becomes the team's shared memory of what the Street said, and email is only its first input.
1406	
1407	| Order | What gets built | Why it matters |
1408	| --- | --- | --- |
1409	| Next | Read-only connection to real mail, run in shadow mode beside one analyst, with a weekly sample of suppressed items to confirm. | Measures recall on real mail before anyone relies on it. |
1410	| Next | Research-log and model integration: accepted changes write to the real model, and thesis records live in the research system. | Closes the loop from email to model for real. |
1411	| Then | All four calendar modes, including first-take cards minutes after a print and a scheduling agent for conference season. | The workflow follows the market calendar. |
1412	| Then | Other inputs join the same ledger: filings, transcripts, expert-call notes and channel checks. | Stitches triage into the fund's other research workflows. |
1413	| Later | Team layer: a PM digest across the four analysts, and read-throughs routed to whichever analyst covers the affected name. | The book belongs to the fund, not one analyst. |
1414	| Later | Source track record: brokers and vendors scored on whether their past claims proved right. | Ranking improves from outcomes, not opinions. |
1415	
1416	Three things need owners before any real deployment: compliance sign-off on the quarantine rule, retention of every decision for audit, and enforcement of research entitlements in the team layer.
1417	
1418	## Decisions needed
1419	
1420	The coding agent uses each default below until told otherwise.
1421	
1422	| # | Question | Default |
1423	| --- | --- | --- |
1424	| 1 | Is the example book acceptable? | Yes. It lives only in the seed files and this document, never in the corpus prompt. |
1425	| 2 | Who supplies the tuning set? | It is generated outside the build into `data/corpus/tuning/`. Until it exists, tuning is pending. |
1426	| 3 | What do the criteria files start with? | The prompt's definition for each label and no more than four starter rules. Further rules are added through the criteria check. |
1427	| 4 | Is the rule-proposal prompt used? | No. It shows tuning labels to a model, so new rules are written by hand unless the reviewer opts in. |
1428	| 5 | Which embedding model? | A Hugging Face model run locally, named by `EMBEDDING_MODEL` in `.env`; default `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5`. |
1429	| 6 | Which model writes attention notes? | Claude Haiku 4.5, through OpenRouter. |
1430	| 7 | Which model runs extraction and the analysis agent? | Claude Sonnet 5.5, through OpenRouter. |
1431	| 8 | Are two skills enough for the prototype? | Yes: alter an existing thesis, and spawn a new thesis. |
1432	| 9 | Which trading dates does the corpus use? | `day_1` is Tuesday, Oct 13, 2026, `day_2` is Wednesday, Oct 14, 2026, and the tuning set is Thursday, Oct 15, 2026. |
1433	| 10 | How deep is the model? | 23 drivers, one forward year, four formulas. |
1434	| 11 | What if the annual reports cannot be fetched? | Use labeled placeholder base figures and report it. |
1435	| 12 | Where do accepted changes persist? | Server memory per visitor session, with a reset button. |
1436	| 13 | What can the live route accept? | Six preset emails, plus free paste under the character cap. |
1437	| 14 | How much tuning is in scope? | The thresholds under "Starting values" and hand-written criteria rules. Prompt optimization only if time remains. |
1438	| 15 | Which coding agent and host? | Claude Code, deploying one container to a Python host. |
1439	
1440	
1441	
1442
